subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: kb/Work PB922 (wave 42) - RULE (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.3 'EXCEPTION-OBJECT shall not be specified as a receiving operand'): OK, SR1. SR1 is a rule about EVERY receiving operand in the language, and only SET had an arm for it, so MOVE U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT drew COBOL1639 ('is not defined - Check the spelling, or declare the item') beside COBOL0901 ('is a reserved word and cannot be used as a user-defined word') - two diagnostics that contradict each other, and neither of them the rule the program broke. Now screened at the ONE general receiving chokepoint, ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving, as COBOL2196 quoting SR1; SET's own arm draws the SAME code and its clause number was repaired from 8.4.3.6 (where cite.py --check FAILS) to 8.4.3.6.3. THE EDITION IS PART OF THE RULE and is measured on both sides: 8.9 reserves the word only from COBOL-2002, so at --std 85 EXCEPTION-OBJECT is an ordinary user-defined word and '01 EXCEPTION-OBJECT PIC X(4).' + 'MOVE "ABCD" TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT' is conforming source that runs (conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb922_exception_object_user_word_85); the one predicate ReferenceResolver.IsExceptionObjectRegister carries spelling, form (8.4.3.6.2's general format is the bare word) and edition together, so no caller can hold a different opinion. editions names 2002 and later because that is where the prohibition applies at all.
